newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian government wins second confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Romanian government wins second confidence vote.

text.p: Romania's centrist government easily defeated a leftist challenge in parliament on Monday and vowed to push ahead with its six month of program of IMF-backed reforms.

"You can put forward as many motions as you like -- we will proceed," Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea told the former communists of the Party for Social Democracy, who were voted out of office last November.
A joint session of parliament's two chambers rejected the opposition no confidence motion by 268 votes to 152 -- much the same margin as a similar vote on Friday.

Ciorbea, who denounced his detractors as "liars, hypocrites and demagogues", has won backing from the International Monetary Fund and World Bank for his policies of freeing prices, liberalising financial markets, reducing subsidies and budget austerity.
But a law on portfolio investment ran into trouble on Monday as investors said amendments to the text would turn Romania into an unattractive prospect.
